Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# ARC: rectangle rays stopped by markers

## Recognition
Use this rule when the input contains a solid axis-aligned rectangle of color 2, sparse isolated markers of one other color (often 1, 3, or 8), and otherwise-zero background. Demonstrations show the rectangle kept in place while color-2 lines are extended outward from its four sides along all of its rows and columns.

## Transformation

3. For each row `r0..r1`, extend color 2 horizontally from the rectangle toward each grid edge. If a marker lies on that row on a given side, do not extend on that side; the marker blocks that outward ray. Otherwise fill every cell from the rectangle edge to that grid edge with 2.
4. For each column `c0..c1`, extend color 2 vertically toward top and bottom edges. A marker in that column beyond the rectangle blocks extension on that side; otherwise fill the intervening cells through the grid edge with 2.
5. Never overwrite markers. Do not extend from markers that are not aligned with a rectangle row/column, and do not add any perpendicular lines at their intersections.

A marker in one direction only blocks that side's ray; it does not block extension in the opposite direction from the rectangle.
